summary: Tested iteration 9's architecture change: Telegram poller now embedded in FastAPI startup/shutdown events instead of a standalone supervisor program. Verified: /api/bot/status healthy, real /start still triggers postback+reply (via live log traffic), /api/r bridge redirect correct (<=64 char start payload), admin PIN unlock + PUT /api/settings + persistence + 401-without-JWT all pass, supervisorctl confirms telegram_bot program removed and backend RUNNING. Stress-tested hot-reload by touching server.py twice consecutively: logs show clean 'Application is stopping'/'Application.stop() complete' then 'Application started' each time, with NO telegram.error.Conflict occurring during or after my triggered reloads (an earlier, unrelated Conflict at 17:09:35 predates my test window and did not recur). Real /start commands processed successfully after reload settled (confirmed via log + db counters). Found one real (non-blocking) bug: PTB's post_init hook is never invoked because start_bot() uses app.initialize()+app.start()+updater.start_polling() instead of run_polling(), and python-telegram-bot's initialize() docstring explicitly states post_init is only called by run_polling()/run_webhook(). Confirmed via db.bot_meta.runtime.started_at staying frozen at the very first boot time (16:57:50) across two live reloads, and no 'bot @tamil_best_service_bot online' log line appearing after any restart.

minor.issue: post_init callback (sets bot description/short description/menu button, creates postback/click indexes, writes db.bot_meta.runtime with fresh started_at) is registered via Application.builder().post_init(post_init) but never executes, because start_bot() calls app.initialize()+app.start()+updater.start_polling() manually instead of app.run_polling(). PTB's Application.initialize() docstring explicitly states: 'Does *not* call post_init - that is only done by run_polling() and run_webhook()'. Verified empirically: db.bot_meta.runtime.started_at stayed at the original first-boot timestamp across two live hot-reloads triggered during this test, and no 'bot @tamil_best_service_bot online' log line appeared after either restart (task explicitly asked to confirm this line appears). Functional impact today is low (indexes/meta/description were already set on the very first-ever boot and are idempotent), but it means: (1) /api/bot/status's 'online' semantics is really just 'has ever booted once, ever' rather than 'this current process is healthy', weakening the exact uptime-confidence signal the anxious user is asking for; (2) if bot description/commands/menu button are ever changed in code, they will silently stop being pushed to Telegram on redeploy.

action_items: In bot.py start_bot(), explicitly call `await post_init(app)` right after `await app.initialize()` (since it's not auto-invoked by initialize()/start()), OR keep a small wrapper that updates db.bot_meta.runtime with a fresh started_at directly inside start_bot() so /api/bot/status genuinely reflects the current process's boot time after every restart -- this closes the gap between the intended monitoring signal and what's actually happening.

Optional: add a lightweight periodic heartbeat write to db.bot_meta (e.g. in a background task) so /api/bot/status's 'online' can reflect true current liveness rather than a single historical write, since that's the crux of the user's original 24/7-uptime complaint.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 9 confirms the big architecture change (embedded poller in FastAPI lifecycle) works and specifically does NOT reproduce the feared post-reload Conflict loop -- that's the headline good news for the user's uptime complaint. The one gap found is post_init never running on restart (PTB quirk: initialize()/start() skip it, only run_polling()/run_webhook() call it) -- low functional impact today but worth patching so /api/bot/status's freshness signal and bot metadata pushes stay accurate across every future redeploy. All auth/bridge/status endpoints and PIN flow remain regression-free vs iterations 7-8.
rca of the issue: post_init is a python-telegram-bot Application-level hook that is documented to only be invoked by the high-level convenience methods run_polling()/run_webhook(), not by the low-level initialize()/start() pair used here to enable running the poller inside an existing asyncio loop (required to embed it in FastAPI's startup event). The main agent's refactor correctly solved the supervisor-dependency problem but didn't carry over post_init's side effects (bot_meta refresh, description/menu setup, index creation) into the new manual init path. Fix: call `await post_init(app)` explicitly inside start_bot() right after app.initialize().
